economic_rationale: Quality-Minus-Junk (Asness-Frazzini-Pedersen 2019 JFE). High-quality firms (profitable, safe, growing) are systematically underpriced relative to junk because investors over-extrapolate distress and under-pay for stable cash generation; the quality premium is a compensation for the willingness to hold boring, slow firms during euphoria. In KR this manifests as a defensive/crisis-hedge tilt rather than a strong unconditional premium (see AX-004): single-axis profitability fails long-only, but the multi-axis profitability+safety+growth composite preserves the crisis-conditional payoff. Mechanism is fundamental (balance-sheet/income-statement) and therefore structurally orthogonal to STR_1715 (earnings-revision/price momentum core) and D (size/microstructure ML).
redundancy_note: Distinct from STR_1715 defense sleeve which uses only Q07_Earnings_Stability + Q25_Ohlson_O (2 of 15 QMJ proxies). QMJ here is a full 3-axis composite (profitability+safety+growth) — measured cor vs STR_1715 score_eff = 0.246 (<0.30). Distinct from D microstructure (cor 0.204).

factor_specs.formula: cross-sectional mean of Z_Score_Aligned over >=2 available profitability proxies, then re-standardized
factor_specs.neutralization: none (composite measured raw; direction via IC Usable_Date<=sig_date, C13/C14)
factor_specs.economic_rationale: profitability premium (Novy-Marx 2013 GPA; cash-based OP Ball et al 2016)

factor_specs.formula: cross-sectional mean of Z_Score_Aligned over >=2 available safety proxies, then re-standardized
factor_specs.economic_rationale: low default risk + earnings stability + low accruals (Sloan 1996; Ohlson 1980)

factor_specs.formula: cross-sectional mean of Z_Score_Aligned over >=2 available growth proxies, then re-standardized
factor_specs.economic_rationale: sustainable growth of quality metrics (AFP 2019 growth axis)

composite_construction.method: equal-axis weighting (AFP 2019): qmj = (prof_z + safe_z + grow_z)/3, then cross-sectional re-standardize
composite_construction.inclusion_rule: require >=2 proxies present per axis AND all 3 axes present per name
composite_construction.ax004_note: multi-axis quality composite (15 proxies across 3 axes) — NOT single GP/single cash-profitability. AX-004 EXCLUSION condition met.

graduation_assessment.verdict: QMJ FAILS Discovery->Deployment graduation as a STANDALONE alpha (rank_IC<0.04, harvey_t<3.0, DSR<0.5, subperiod<0.5, recent-period IC negative). However it is a GENUINE 4th-orthogonal diversifier (cor<0.30 vs both STR_1715 and D) with strong crisis-conditional behavior (AX-001 v2 ratio 8.1, ic_bad 0.100) and ultra-low turnover (1.0/yr). Its value proposition is as a defensive 4th sleeve in a multi-sleeve blend (AX-007 exception), NOT as an independent admit.

challenge_flags.note: recent 3Y (2020-LB) IC = -0.007, NEGATIVE vs overall 0.026 — quality premium decayed/reversed in KR recent regime (consistent with KR lottery/skewness anomaly reversal, memory learning_kr_lottery_anomaly_reversal). Standalone use unsafe.
quintile returns plateau at top (Q3 0.00835 > Q5 0.00823) — best-quality names do not beat merely-good. Long top-20 selection mechanism weak (AX-004 caution).
portfolio_alpha_t_net=0.63 << IC harvey_t=2.68. Per Cycle 2 lesson, portfolio-alpha t is authoritative for sleeve viability — standalone sleeve statistically insignificant.
Despite standalone failure, orthogonality (cor 0.25/0.20) + crisis ratio 8.1 + TO 1.0/yr make QMJ a credible defensive 4th-sleeve candidate for multi-sleeve blend, subject to optimizer sizing.
